content: 1. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of diltiazem by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of doravirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and development of resistance. 3. Co-administration of doravirine with strong CYP3A4 inducers may significantly reduce doravirine plasma concentrations, leading to a loss of virologic response and potential resistance. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Nafcillin reduces the efficacy of dostarlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised, as this may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 5. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of doxorubicin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended, as strong CYP3A4 inducers can increase the metabolism of CYP3A4 substrates. 6. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of liposomal doxorubicin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised, as strong CYP3A4 inducers may increase the metabolism of CYP3A4 substrates. 7. Doxycycline reduces the efficacy of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used, as bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 8. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of dronabinol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended, as dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. 9. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of dronedarone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Nafcillin decreases the efficacy of durvalumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised, as this may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 11. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of duvelisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used, as co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers decreases duvelisib exposure and may reduce its efficacy. 12. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended, as strong CYP3A4 inducers may increase the metabolism of CYP3A4 substrates. 13. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of elacestrant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 14. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 15. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used, as moderate CYP3A inducers may reduce the therapeutic effect of elbasvir/grazoprevir. 16. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of eliglustat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended, as strong CYP3A inducers significantly reduce eliglustat exposure. 17. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used, as co-administration with CYP3A inducers may lead to decreased plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and potential loss of therapeutic effect or resistance. 18. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to loss of virologic response and resistance. 19. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of encorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 20. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of entrectinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 21. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of enzalutamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of erdafitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 23. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of erlotinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 24. Erythromycin base reduces the efficacy of nafcillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 25. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 26. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 27. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 28. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of escitalopram by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 29. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 30. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 31. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 32. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of esterified estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 33. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of estropipate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 34. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of eszopiclone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 35. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 36. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of ethosuximide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 37. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of etoposide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 38. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of etravirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 39. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of eucalyptus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 40. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of everolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 41. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of exemestane by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 42. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of fedratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used, as the effect of co-administering a strong CYP3A4 inducer with fedratinib has not been studied. 43. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of felbamate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 44. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of fentanyl by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may lead to decreased fentanyl plasma concentrations, lack of efficacy, or withdrawal syndrome in patients with physical dependence. After stopping a CYP3A4 inducer, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, potentially prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. Close monitoring is required. 45. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of fentanyl intranasal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions as above apply. 46. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of fentanyl transdermal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions as above apply. 47. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of fentanyl transmucosal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar precautions as above apply. 48. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of fesoterodine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 49. Nafcillin increases the plasma levels or effects of fexinidazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used, as increased plasma concentrations of its active metabolite (M2) are associated with QT prolongation risks. 50. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of finerenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 51. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of flibanserin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended, as strong CYP3A4 inducers substantially decrease flibanserin systemic exposure. 52. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of flurazepam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 53. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 54. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of fostamatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 55. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of fostemsavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it significantly decreases the active moiety (temsavir) plasma concentrations, potentially leading to loss of virologic response and resistance. 56. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of fruquintinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, continue fruquintinib at the recommended dosage. 57. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of ganaxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose, but do not exceed the maximum daily dose for weight. 58. Nafcillin decreases the plasma levels or effects of gefitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is required, increasing gefitinib to 500 mg daily if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. Resume the standard dose of 250 mg/day seven days after discontinuing the inducer. 59. Nafcillin reduces the plasma levels or effects of glasdegib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used.
